extra_misconceptions.fact: In-water recompression risks drowning and worsening hypoxia; administer 100 percent surface oxygen and evacuate to a hyperbaric chamber.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Descending back underwater is the safest field treatment when a diver develops joint pain after surfacing.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Alcohol and folk remedies trigger unspent nematocysts to fire more venom; rinse with vinegar or seawater and immerse in hot water.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Applying meat tenderizer or rubbing alcohol neutralizes jellyfish nematocysts on a stung diver's skin.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Deep rapid breathing purges carbon dioxide without adding significant oxygen, delaying the urge to breathe and risking shallow-water blackout.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hyperventilating rapidly before a dive doubles the oxygen stored in a diver's blood and lungs.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Medication can wear off at depth and cause a reverse block on ascent, trapping expanding air inside the middle ear or sinuses.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Taking decongestant pills right before a deep dive prevents ear and sinus squeezes for the entire trip.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to nitrogen narcosis symptoms when a diver ascends a few yards to shallower water?
Which physical indicator distinguishes arterial gas embolism from slower-onset decompression sickness on the boat?
Why is it dangerous to forcefully pinch your nose and blow after an ear squeeze has already started?
What flow rate of pure oxygen should a rescuer deliver to a breathing diver suspected of decompression illness?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Equipment can malfunction or be lost in surf, requiring a diver to tread water and swim to safety using personal watermanship alone.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Fins and an inflatable buoyancy vest eliminate the need for strong unassisted swimming skills in open water.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scouts must earn the complete Swimming merit badge before beginning requirements 3 through 6 of the Scuba Diving merit badge.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Passing the basic BSA swimmer classification test satisfies the prerequisite for the Scuba Diving merit badge.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sprinting against a current causes rapid exhaustion and carbon dioxide buildup; swim calmly parallel to shore until out of the flow.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Swimming fast with a high kick rate is the best way to make headway when caught in a coastal rip current.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Requirement 2 mandates earning the Swimming merit badge before starting any of requirements 3 through 6 for Scuba Diving.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Completing the open-water scuba certification dives first allows a Scout to finish the Swimming merit badge afterward.

extra_socratic_questions: What measurement confirms that a Scout has met the continuous distance and stroke proficiency standards of the Swimming badge?
Why is it dangerous to rely solely on a buoyancy compensator when your mask floods or a fin strap breaks at the surface?
Which physical indicator during a 150-yard swim shows a Scout has the aerobic pacing needed to fight a surface current?
Where should a Scout record the completion date of the Swimming merit badge before scheduling confined-water scuba training?

extra_misconceptions.fact: A shore observer cannot share air or clear an entanglement at depth; the code requires diving with a buddy from entry to exit.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Diving solo in calm, shallow water is acceptable under the Scuba Diver's Code if an observer waits on shore.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Skip-breathing causes dangerous carbon dioxide retention and headaches, and any pause in breathing during ascent risks lung overexpansion.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Breathing slowly and skipping inhalations underwater is a safe method to stretch a tank of air longer.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Overweighting forces you to overinflate your vest and increases air consumption; proper weighting lets you hover at eye level with empty lungs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Neutral buoyancy means adding maximum lead weight to your belt so you never float toward the surface.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Computers can fail or differ in conservatism, so buddies must agree on depth, time, and minimum turn pressure before entering the water.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Relying entirely on a wrist dive computer removes the need to plan a maximum depth and bottom time with your buddy.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the microscopic air spaces inside lung alveoli if a diver holds their breath during an ascent?
Under what condition does the Scuba Diver's Code require you to cancel or abort a dive even after reaching the dive site?
What pressure-gauge reading confirms a diver is returning to the surface with a safe reserve of breathing gas?
Where should a Scout position themselves relative to rising exhaust bubbles when ascending to the surface?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Introductory resort courses are not full certifications; a Scout must complete academic, pool, and four open-water checkout dives.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Finishing a resort discover-scuba experience in a pool fulfills Requirement 4 for the Scuba Diving merit badge.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scouting America recognizes specific agencies such as PADI, NAUI, SSI, SDI, YMCA, and PDIC that meet Recreational Scuba Training Council rules.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any international dive club card qualifies a Scout for the merit badge regardless of Scouting America scuba policy.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Open Water certification is strictly limited to no-decompression recreational depths with direct vertical access to the surface.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Open Water Diver certification qualifies a Scout to enter overhead cavern ceilings, shipwrecks, and decompression depths.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Youth certified as Junior Open Water Divers must dive with a certified adult according to agency standards and Scouting America barriers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Junior Open Water certified Scouts may dive with another underage buddy without an adult certified diver present.

extra_socratic_questions: Which training agencies are explicitly recognized under the Scouting America scuba policy for Open Water certification?
What depth limit applies to a Junior Open Water Diver aged 12 to 14 compared to an adult Open Water Diver?
What happens to a diver's buoyancy during a three-minute safety stop at 15 feet as tank air is breathed down?
Which emergency gas-sharing and mask-clearing skills must a student demonstrate in open water to earn certification?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Corals are fragile colonies of living invertebrate polyps that depend on symbiotic algae and die when abraded by fins or hands.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Reef corals are inert mineral rocks that only provide shelter for fish rather than living animals themselves.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Stratified lakes form distinct thermal layers called thermoclines where temperature drops sharply and visibility often changes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Freshwater lakes and quarries have uniform water temperature and visibility from the surface to the bottom.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Saltwater is denser than freshwater, so a diver wearing the same exposure suit needs additional weight to descend in the ocean.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dive weights needed for neutral buoyancy in a freshwater quarry remain identical when diving in ocean saltwater.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sand patches house camouflaged rays and invertebrates, and kicking up sediment smothers nearby coral polyps and ruins visibility.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standing on sandy patches between coral heads is a harmless way for a tired diver to rest on the bottom.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a kelp forest ecosystem when sea urchins multiply unchecked after their natural predators decline?
Which physical indicator marks the thermocline boundary when a diver descends into a temperate freshwater quarry or lake?
Why is it dangerous to fin vertically or drag a submersible pressure gauge across a tropical coral reef?
Under what condition does an estuary experience rapid shifts in visibility, salinity, and water density during a dive?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Commercial diving requires specialized trade school certification, surface-supplied helmet gear training, and OSHA compliance.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Earning a recreational Divemaster rating qualifies a diver to perform commercial underwater welding and bridge repair.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Research institutions operate under American Academy of Underwater Sciences standards requiring medical exams and 100 hours of training.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Scientific divers at universities and aquariums only need an Open Water card to log official research dives.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scuba careers span marine biology, underwater photography, public safety recovery, aquarium husbandry, and hyperbaric medicine.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Teaching scuba classes is the only viable full-time career path available within the diving industry.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Police and fire dive teams operate in zero-visibility, contaminated water with tether communications and full-face masks.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Public safety divers work in clear, warm water under the same conditions practiced during recreational resort courses.

extra_socratic_questions: What minimum number of logged dives and rescue certifications must a diver complete before entering Divemaster training?
Which technical distinction separates a recreational scuba instructor from a surface-supplied commercial salvage diver?
Why is it dangerous to attempt public safety search-and-recovery dives using only recreational Open Water training?
What academic credentials and scientific diving standards must a marine biologist meet to conduct underwater research?
